business_ops.seasonality: Demand for the Company's products is dependent on the demand for end products manufactured by its OEM customers and is subject to seasonality and cyclicality, which may result in fluctuations in sales volumes, uneven revenue recognition and variations in capacity utilization across fiscal quarters. Quarter-wise share of revenue from operations: Q1 (April-June) 24.35% (Fiscal 2026), 21.96% (Fiscal 2025), 26.40% (Fiscal 2024); Q2 (July-September) 16.81%, 17.51%, 15.45%; Q3 (October-December) 26.36%, 24.41%, 21.93%; Q4 (January-March) 32.49%, 36.12%, 36.23%. The DRHP states these seasonal fluctuations may adversely impact cash flows, working capital requirements and inventory management.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration: by building an in-house brass manufacturing, forging and extrusion facility at Noida Facility 1, the Company states it has integrated backward to ensure quality and supply control. It manufactures brass billets and rods using brass alloys primarily comprising copper and zinc, which are further processed into forged components, extruded sections and brass machining parts in accordance with customer specifications; the forged and extruded products are then subjected to machining operations such as turning, drilling, tapping and threading to achieve required dimensions and tolerances. Through this integrated process the Company converts brass into forging parts and machined components within its own manufacturing facilities and manages raw material processing and component production internally. Inputs: primary raw materials are brass scrap, brass honey scrap, copper tubes, copper rods, aluminium rods and consumables such as zinc ingots, flux and oil, procured from domestic and international suppliers on a purchase order basis; the risk factors also list steel round bar and aluminium solid rod. During Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 raw materials were imported from 7 countries - South Korea, Vietnam, Thailand, China, Japan, Italy and the United Kingdom. Domestic purchases were 90.29% (Fiscal 2026), 74.74% (Fiscal 2025) and 54.82% (Fiscal 2024) of purchases, with import purchases at 9.71%, 25.26% and 45.18% respectively. The Company usually does not enter into long-term supply contracts with raw material suppliers; pricing and production volumes are negotiated for each purchase order. High-precision machinery (automatic tube cutting machine, integrated CNC bending machine, automatic forming machine, automatic brazing machine, linear 5-axis brazing machine, transfer machining centre, forging machine, packing line, brass melting furnace, brass extrusion press, forging press) is sourced from domestic and international machinery manufacturers in China and South Korea. Outbound, finished goods are transported by road, sea and air on CIF or FOB terms through third-party transportation and logistics providers. Facilities are spread across five strategically located sites in India at Noida, Neemrana, Pune, Bengaluru and Sanand covering a total area of 32,351.84 square meters, and inventory is managed through Sofgen, an ERP system.

overview.business_model: The Company manufactures components of specific sizes, dimensions, configurations and metal grades from brass scrap, brass honey scrap, copper tubes, steel round bar and other consumable materials such as aluminium solid rod and zinc ingots, and sells them to Original Equipment Manufacturers. Its HVAC components primarily comprise Copper Tube U & C Bends and Copper Tube RAC Indoor and Outdoor Assemblies, which are used in heat exchangers and refrigerant circuit assemblies across heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration systems. End-industries served include white goods (HVAC & Refrigerator), electrical equipment manufacturing, tubing components and fittings, metal manufacturing and others including testing and calibration, energy, plastic and rubber. Named customers include LG Electronics (India) Limited, Haier Appliances (India) Private Limited, Bosch Home Comfort India Limited, Daikin Airconditioning India Private Limited and Ecofrost Technologies Private Limited. The main objects clause also permits job work, contract manufacturing, technical collaboration and R&D for OEMs and allied industries.

They may take or block actions that conflict with the interests of the Company or minority shareholders, including actions that delay, defer or cause a change of control or a change in capital structure. Concentration of ownership may also delay, prevent or deter a change in control, and a substantial sale of shares by them could adversely affect the market price.
compliance_legal.evidence: "We cannot assure you that our Promoters and Promoter Group members will act to resolve any conflicts of interest in our favour."
compliance_legal.title: Promoters and Promoter Group will retain significant control after the Offer

compliance_legal.detail: Risk factor 51. As a listed company the Company will incur significant legal, accounting, corporate governance and other expenses not incurred as an unlisted company, and will be subject to the SEBI Listing Regulations requiring audited annual and unaudited quarterly reports. Maintaining and improving disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting will require significant resources and management attention, and additional legal and accounting staff may need to be hired.
compliance_legal.evidence: "We are not a publicly listed company and have not, historically, been subjected to the increased scrutiny of our affairs by shareholders, regulators and the public at large that is associated with being a listed company."
compliance_legal.title: Requirements of being a publicly listed company may strain resources

compliance_legal.detail: Risk factor 52. The Directors do not have experience of holding directorship in a listed company and accordingly have limited exposure to management of the affairs of a listed company, which entails several compliance requirements and scrutiny by shareholders, regulators and the public. The Board may have to give increased attention to such procedures, diverting attention from business operations.
compliance_legal.evidence: "None of our Directors on our board possess experience of being on the board of a listed company."
compliance_legal.title: No Director on the Board has experience of serving on the board of a listed company

compliance_legal.detail: Risk factor 55 (External Risk Factors). The regulatory and policy environment is evolving. The Government of India has introduced the Code on Social Security, 2020, the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and the Code on Wages, 2019, which came into force pursuant to a Ministry of Labour and Employment notification dated November 21, 2025; draft implementation rules have been recently notified and the Company has not yet fully assessed their impact. The Code on Wages, 2019 restricts the portion of wages that can be excluded from employment-benefit calculations to a maximum of 50% of total wages. Environmental, safety, health and labour regulations impose controls on air and water discharge and may cause regulators to require shutdown of manufacturing facilities.
compliance_legal.evidence: Labour Codes "have come into force pursuant to notification by Ministry of Labour and Employment dated November 21, 2025". Also cited: a Supreme Court of India decision clarifying components of basic wages for provident fund payments, which resulted in an increase in provident fund payments by companies.
compliance_legal.title: Changing laws, rules and regulations, including the new Labour Codes and adverse application of tax laws

compliance_legal.detail: Risk factor 59 (External Risk Factors). The Competition Act regulates practices having an appreciable adverse effect on competition (AAEC) in India; agreements causing AAEC are void and may attract substantial penalties, and abuse of dominant position is prohibited. Combination provisions in force since June 1, 2011 require notification to and pre-approval by the Competition Commission of India above prescribed asset and turnover thresholds. The CCI has extra-territorial powers. The DRHP states that because the Company pursues an acquisition driven growth strategy, it may be affected directly or indirectly by the application or interpretation of the Competition Act or by CCI enforcement proceedings.
compliance_legal.evidence: "However, since we pursue an acquisition driven growth strategy, we may be affected, directly or indirectly, by the application or interpretation of any provision of the Competition Act."
compliance_legal.title: Exposure to the Competition Act, 2002 and CCI enforcement

compliance_legal.detail: Risk factor 71. Transfers of shares between non-residents and residents are freely permitted subject to compliance with RBI pricing guidelines and reporting requirements; non-compliance or falling within exceptions requires prior RBI approval. Shareholders seeking to convert rupee sale proceeds into foreign currency and repatriate them require a no objection / tax clearance certificate from the income tax authority. There is no assurance that required approvals can be obtained on any particular terms or at all.
compliance_legal.evidence: "We cannot assure investors that any required approval from the RBI or any other Indian government agency can be obtained on any particular terms, or at all."
compliance_legal.title: Foreign investment restrictions under Indian law

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 7. Working capital is required to finance raw material purchases and other expenses before customer payment is received. Actual future capital requirements may differ from estimates due to unforeseen delays, cost overruns, regulatory changes and technological changes. Working capital needs may increase if payment terms lengthen, raising receivables and short-term borrowings. Additional debt financing would increase interest obligations, may impose restrictive covenants, increase the debt-to-equity ratio and require charges or liens on assets.
financial_valuation.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Total current assets excluding cash and bank balances 15,056.72 (FY2026), 11,311.49 (FY2025), 9,272.46 (FY2024); total current liabilities excluding borrowings and lease liability 5,257.48, 3,540.86, 4,135.64; net working capital 9,799.24, 7,770.63, 5,136.82; working capital as % of revenue from operations 20.93, 19.97, 17.03. Capital expenditure in manufacturing activities ₹2,693.77 lakhs, ₹2,437.48 lakhs and ₹1,574.64 lakhs, representing 42.45%, 45.14% and 33.90% of Property, Plant and Equipment.
financial_valuation.title: Substantial capital and working capital requirements; may need additional financing

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 8. Price and availability of brass scrap, brass honey scrap, copper tubes, steel round bar and consumables are subject to volatility from global and domestic demand-supply dynamics, logistics and manufacturing costs, inflation, government regulations, production levels, competition, duties and taxes, trade restrictions, transportation costs and currency movements. Raw materials are procured on tentative customer projections; a quarterly pricing model is followed for both procurement and sales. If cost increases cannot be passed on, or if price increases cause customers to reduce, delay or cancel orders, results could be materially affected.
financial_valuation.title: Cost of goods sold was 82.84% of total expenses in Fiscal 2026; exposure to raw material price volatility

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 11. Borrowing facilities are rated by a credit rating agency from time to time. A downgrade, inability to obtain a rating in a timely manner, non-availability of ratings, or poor ratings could increase borrowing costs, give lenders the right to review facilities availed and adversely affect access to capital and debt markets. There was no downgrade during the last three Fiscals.
financial_valuation.evidence: CRISIL Ratings Limited — Fiscal 2024 (February 12, 2024 and March 11, 2024): CRISIL BBB/Stable (long term), CRISIL A3+ (short term). Fiscal 2025: no rating shown. Fiscal 2026 (June 6, 2025 and July, 2025): CRISIL BBB+/Stable (long term), CRISIL A2 (short term).
financial_valuation.title: Adverse revision to credit rating could raise borrowing costs and restrict access to capital

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 12. Financing agreements contain restrictive covenants requiring lender consent for, among others, reorganisation/amalgamation, investment or lending, change in constitution, control, ownership, shareholding pattern, capital structure or management, issuance of corporate guarantees for group entities, declaration or payment of dividend, change in nature of business, amendments to the memorandum and articles of association and creation of encumbrances. Secured borrowings require charge over existing and future fixed assets, cash and cash equivalents, hypothecation over current assets including inventory, work-in-progress, finished goods, book debts and receivables, movable and immovable assets, plant and machinery, plus personal guarantees from the Promoters. Current debt facilities carry floating or base-rate-linked interest. The Company states it is currently in compliance with financial covenants.
financial_valuation.evidence: Total outstanding borrowings as of March 31, 2026: ₹9,654.71 lakhs. Debt-to-equity ratio 1.02 times (FY2026), 0.90 times (FY2025), 0.91 times (FY2024). Finance cost (₹ in lakhs) 757.79 / 1.70% of total expenses (FY2026), 603.17 / 1.66% (FY2025), 491.07 / 1.68% (FY2024).
financial_valuation.title: Total outstanding borrowings of ₹9,654.71 lakhs with restrictive covenants and floating interest rates

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 14. Financial statements are presented in Indian Rupees while revenues and operating expenses are influenced by the currency of the countries of sale and raw material import. The DRHP notes that because the Company both imports and exports in the same currency, fluctuations have offsetting effects, reducing overall exposure, but states the Indian rupee depreciated against the U.S. dollar over the last five years.
financial_valuation.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Foreign Exchange Fluctuation Gain (Net) 110.12 / 0.24% of revenue from operations (FY2026), 107.93 / 0.28% (FY2025), 72.66 / 0.24% (FY2024). Foreign currency exposure (Note 32): Import Creditors USD 6.89 / INR 622.07 (2025-26), USD 12.91 / INR 1,131.60 (2024-25), USD 30.17 / INR 2,563.71 (2023-24); Export Debtors USD 2.23 / INR 211.46, USD 2.90 / INR 248.58, USD 1.62 / INR 132.96.
financial_valuation.title: Exposure to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 19. The Company has experienced negative net cash flows from investing activities and may continue to do so. Negative cash flows over extended periods, or significant negative cash flows in the short term, may impair the ability to operate the business and implement growth plans, meet working capital expenditure and repay loans without external finance.
financial_valuation.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Net cash from/(used in) operating activities 1,156.84 (FY2026), 1,206.62 (FY2025), 1,671.93 (FY2024). Net cash from/(used in) investing activities (2,716.85), (2,705.56), (1,825.44). Net cash from/(used in) financing activities 1,568.72, 1,516.16, 18.57.
financial_valuation.title: Negative net cash flows from investing activities in each of the last three Fiscals

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 36. Sales to customers are on an open credit basis with a standard payment period of between 43 days and 49 days. The DRHP discloses that there have been instances of delays in payments by some customers in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, though such receivables are expected to be realised in the normal course and have not been treated as impaired. Estimates of the allowance for doubtful receivables may not prove accurate.
financial_valuation.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Trade receivables 7,004.69 (FY2026), 4,947.85 (FY2025), 4,136.63 (FY2024). Trade receivables days 47, 43, 49. Bad debts written off 26.75 (FY2026, 0.06% of revenue from operations), 1.19 (FY2025, negligible), 0.20 (FY2024, negligible). Revenue from operations 46,808.59, 38,907.79, 30,170.42.
financial_valuation.title: Receivables collection risk; instances of delayed payment by customers

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 37. As on March 31, 2026 the Company had an unsecured loan from Promoter Jignesh Panchal of ₹341.32 lakhs, repayable on demand and capable of being recalled at any time. The DRHP states the arrangement has not been terminated nor repayment demanded as of the date of the DRHP. If recalled, alternative financing may be unavailable on commercially reasonable terms, potentially requiring use of internal accruals, curtailment of working capital or additional indebtedness at higher rates or with more restrictive covenants.
financial_valuation.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Unsecured borrowings 341.32 (FY2026), nil shown (FY2025), 350.00 (FY2024). Total borrowings 9,654.71 (FY2026), 5,014.62 (FY2024). Unsecured borrowings as % of total borrowings 3.54 (FY2026), 6.98 (FY2024).
financial_valuation.title: Unsecured loan of ₹341.32 lakhs from Promoter repayable on demand

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 42. The DRHP states there is no assurance the Company will experience similar growth in future fiscal years, citing dependency on a limited number of customers, the challenge of sustaining similar capacity expansions and high product volumes, and fluctuations in customer demand, market dynamics and competitive pressures.
financial_valuation.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Revenue from operations 46,808.59 (FY2026), 38,907.79 (FY2025), 30,170.42 (FY2024). Revenue growth (YoY%) 20.31, 28.96, 3.33. Revenue CAGR 24.58%.
financial_valuation.title: Historical revenue growth may not be indicative of future growth

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 43. Contingent liabilities as stated in the Restated Financial Information may crystallise into actual liabilities, in which event business, results of operations, profitability and margins, cash flows and financial condition may be adversely affected. There is no assurance similar or increased levels of contingent liabilities will not be incurred.
financial_valuation.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Demand for Excess ITC Availed in GSTR3B/GSTR9 which is not confirmed in GSTR2B/2A for FY 2023-24: 137.58; Total 137.58 as of March 31, 2026. financial_valuation.title: Contingent liabilities of ₹137.58 lakhs as on March 31, 2026

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 47. The dividend distribution policy was approved and adopted by the Board on May 22, 2026 and dividends were paid for the last three Fiscals. Future dividends will depend on future earnings, cash flows, financial condition, working capital requirements, capital expenditures and applicable Indian legal restrictions; earnings may be retained to finance development and expansion, and financing agreement terms may restrict dividend payments.
financial_valuation.evidence: "The dividend distribution policy of our Company was approved and adopted by our Board on May 22, 2026. Further, we have paid dividend for the last three Fiscals."
financial_valuation.title: No assurance of future dividend payments

The entire proceeds of the Offer for Sale, net of his share of Offer-related expenses, will be paid to him and the Company will receive no proceeds from the Offer for Sale.
financial_valuation.evidence: "The entire proceeds from the Offer for Sale, net of his share of Offer-related expenses, will be paid to our Promoter Selling Shareholder, Jignesh Panchal and our Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer for Sale."
financial_valuation.title: Offer for Sale proceeds accrue to the Promoter Selling Shareholder, not to the Company

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 49. Specified securities were issued in the last 12 months from the date of the DRHP at a price which may be lower than the Offer Price. The DRHP states prices at which Equity Shares were issued in the past year should not be taken as indicative of the Price Band, Offer Price or post-listing trading price.
financial_valuation.evidence: "We have issued specified securities in the last 12 months at a price which may be lower than the Offer Price. For further details, see “Capital Structure” on page 97."
financial_valuation.title: Specified securities issued in the preceding 12 months at a price that may be below the Offer Price

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 50. Non-GAAP measures included are EBITDA, EBITDA Margin, Return on Capital Employed, PAT Margin, Return on Net Worth and Fixed Assets to turnover. These are not required by, or presented in accordance with, Ind AS, Indian GAAP, IFRS or US GAAP, are not standardised terms, may be calculated differently by other companies and are of limited utility as an analytical tool. Methodologies for tracking internal operating metrics may change over time.
financial_valuation.evidence: Non-GAAP Measures listed: "EBITDA, EBITDA Margin, Return on Capital Employed, Pat Margin, Return on Net Worth and Fixed Assets to turnover".
financial_valuation.title: Inclusion of non-GAAP financial measures that may not be comparable across the industry

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 56 (External Risk Factors). The Restated Financial Information for financial years 2026, 2025 and 2024 is prepared under Ind AS notified under the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015 read with Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013. Ind AS differs from other accounting principles, so statements may not be comparable to historical financial statements, and Restated Financial Information may change if new or amended Ind AS standards are issued or elections are revised.
financial_valuation.evidence: "Persons not familiar with Ind AS should limit their reliance on the financial disclosures presented in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus."
financial_valuation.title: Differences between Ind AS and Indian GAAP, IFRS and U.S. GAAP

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 63 (External Risk Factors). Borrowing costs and access to the debt capital markets depend significantly on India's credit ratings; adverse revisions by international rating agencies may impair the ability to raise additional financing on favourable terms and affect the price of the Equity Shares.
financial_valuation.evidence: "Our borrowing costs and our access to the debt capital markets depend significantly on the credit ratings of India."
financial_valuation.title: A downgrade in India's sovereign ratings may affect the trading price of the Equity Shares

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 64 (Risks relating to the Equity Shares and the Offer). The Offer Price is to be determined through a book-building process. The DRHP notes there has been no public market for the Equity Shares prior to the Offer, an active trading market may not develop or be sustained, and any valuation exercise undertaken for the Offer would not be based on a benchmark with industry peers. It also discloses that the current market price of securities listed pursuant to certain previous initial public offerings managed by the Book Running Lead Manager may be below their respective issue prices.
financial_valuation.evidence: "In addition to the above, the current market price of securities listed pursuant to certain previous initial public offerings managed by the Book Running Lead Manager may be below its respective issue prices."
financial_valuation.title: Offer Price may not be indicative of the market price on or after listing

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 65. SEBI and the Stock Exchanges apply GSM where the trading price of a security does not commensurate with financial health and fundamentals such as earnings, book value, fixed assets, net worth, price per equity multiple and market capitalisation, and ASM on securities with surveillance concerns based on price and volume variation and volatility. If triggered, restrictions may include limiting trading frequency (for example, trading allowed once a week or a month) or freezing of price on the upper side.
financial_valuation.evidence: GSM/ASM parameters cited include "net worth and net fixed assets of securities, high low variation in securities, client concentration and close to close price variation."
financial_valuation.title: Possible imposition of Additional Surveillance Measures (ASM) or Graded Surveillance Measures (GSM)

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 66. There has been no public market for the Equity Shares prior to the Offer; the purchase price will be determined by the Company in consultation with the Book Running Lead Manager through the Book Building Process and may not be indicative of the post-Offer market price. Investors may be unable to resell at or above the Offer Price and may lose all or part of their investment.
financial_valuation.evidence: Listed price-influencing factors include "quarterly variations in our results of operations", "results of operations that vary from the expectations of securities analysts and investors", "a change in research analysts' recommendations" and "additions or departures of Key Managerial Personnel".
financial_valuation.title: No assurance that a liquid market for the Equity Shares will develop after listing

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 67. An aggregate of 20% of fully diluted post-Offer capital held by the Promoters will be treated as minimum Promoters' Contribution and locked in for three (3) years, with the balance of Promoter-held Equity Shares locked in for one (1) year from the date of Allotment. Beyond customary lock-in, there is no restriction on disposal of Equity Shares by the Promoters, and future issuances may be at prices below the then trading price or the Offer Price.
financial_valuation.evidence: "an aggregate of 20% of our fully diluted post-Offer capital held by our Promoters shall be considered as minimum Promoters' Contribution and locked in for a period of three (3) years and the balance Equity Shares held by our Promoters following the Offer will be locked-in for one (1) year from the date of Allotment."
financial_valuation.title: Future issuance of Equity Shares or sales by Promoters could dilute holdings and depress the price

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 68. Listing permission is granted only after issue and allotment and submission of relevant documents to the Stock Exchanges. Demat credit is expected within one (1) Working Day of finalisation of the Basis of Allotment; allotment and credit could take approximately three Working Days from the Bid/Offer Closing Date, and trading is expected to commence within three Working Days of that date. Delay in obtaining approval would restrict the ability to dispose of Equity Shares, and interest may be payable if allotment, refunds or demat credits are not made within prescribed periods.
financial_valuation.evidence: "trading in Equity Shares upon receipt of listing and trading approval from the Stock Exchanges, trading of Equity Shares is expected to commence within three Working Days from Bid/ Offer Closing Date."
financial_valuation.title: Inability to sell Equity Shares immediately after purchase in the Offer

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 69. Capital gains on the sale of equity shares in an Indian company are generally taxable in India. The DRHP notes the Union Cabinet has approved the Income Tax Bill, 2025 amending and replacing the Income Tax Act, 1961, and that the Finance Bill 2026 (introduced after the Union Budget for Fiscal 2027 announced on February 1, 2026) received Presidential assent and is notified as the Finance Act, 2026 effective April 1, 2026, proposing changes including reduction of the minimum alternate tax rate, a shift from the old to the new regime for minimum alternate tax, reduction of rates of tax collected at source and taxation of buy-back consideration as capital gains. The effects have not been fully determined.
financial_valuation.evidence: Long-term capital gains exceeding ₹125,000 on listed equity shares held for more than 12 months: 12.5% (plus surcharge and cess), subject to STT. Shares held more than 24 months sold off a recognised stock exchange without STT: 12.5%. Short-term capital gains on shares held 12 months or less: 20% (plus surcharge and cess). Stamp duty on transfer of certain securities: 0.015% on delivery basis and 0.003% on non-delivery basis.
financial_valuation.title: Indian capital gains and dividend taxation on the sale of Equity Shares

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 70. Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, QIBs and Non-Institutional Bidders may not withdraw or lower their Bids in terms of quantity of Equity Shares or Bid Amount at any stage after submitting a Bid; Retail Individual Bidders may revise Bids during the Bid/Offer Period and withdraw until the Bid/Offer Closing Date. Adverse events may occur between Bid submission and Allotment, and the Company may complete Allotment, listing and commencement of trading even if such events occur.
financial_valuation.evidence: Allotment, listing and commencement of trading are required to be completed "within three (3) Working Days from the Bid/ Offer Closing Date".
financial_valuation.title: QIBs and Non-Institutional Bidders cannot withdraw or lower Bids after submission

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 72. The DRHP lists factors that may cause the market price to fluctuate, several of which are beyond the Company's control, including quarterly variations in earnings and those of competitors, failure of securities analysts to cover the Equity Shares, results that vary from analyst expectations or from competitors, changes in expectations of future financial performance, changes in analyst recommendations, announcements of significant acquisitions or capital commitments, activities of suppliers, announcements of significant claims or proceedings, new laws and regulations, additions or departures of key management personnel, changes in exchange rates and general economic and stock market conditions.
financial_valuation.evidence: "Changes in relation to any of the factors listed above could adversely affect the price of the Equity Shares."
financial_valuation.title: Trading volume and market price of the Equity Shares may be volatile following the Offer

financial_valuation.detail: Risk factor 73. Prior to the Offer there has been no public market for the Equity Shares and an active trading market may not develop or be sustained. Listing and quotation do not guarantee that a market will develop or, if developed, its liquidity. The Offer Price determined through the book-building process may not be indicative of the market price at commencement of trading or thereafter, and investors may be unable to resell at or above the Offer Price.
financial_valuation.evidence: "Prior to the Offer, there has been no public market for the Equity Shares, and an active trading market on the Stock Exchanges may not develop or be sustained after the Offer."
financial_valuation.title: Equity Shares have never been publicly traded; price and volume fluctuations may follow the Offer

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 1. The Company served 61, 52 and 61 customers in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 and derives a significant portion of revenue from its top 5 and top 10 customers. Named customers include LG Electronics (India) Limited, Haier Appliances (India) Private Limited, Bosch Home Comfort India Limited, Daikin Airconditioning India Private Limited and Ecofrost Technologies Private Limited; other customer names are withheld for want of consent. The DRHP states loss of any substantial portion of sales to these customers could adversely affect business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows, while noting no such loss occurred in the last three Fiscals.
internal_operational.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Top 5 customers: 39,338.26 / 84.09% (FY2026), 30,769.74 / 79.15% (FY2025), 22,746.95 / 75.45% (FY2024). FY2026 single largest: Daikin Airconditioning India Private Limited 15,623.49 / 33.40%; LG Electronics (India) Limited 7,851.65 / 16.78%; Haier Appliances (India) Private Limited 6,870.94 / 14.69%.
internal_operational.title: Customer concentration: top 5 customers were 84.09% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 2. Financial performance and business stability depend heavily on the sale of HVAC components; the DRHP states other products (VRV, refrigerator, brass components) cannot fully counterbalance negative events affecting HVAC sales, and that a decline in HVAC sales could have a material adverse impact on business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects.
internal_operational.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) HVAC components 36,414.35 / 77.84% (FY2026), 29,412.47 / 75.66% (FY2025), 22,943.73 / 76.11% (FY2024). VRV 6,519.77 / 13.94%; Refrigerator 2,593.70 / 5.54%; Brass 1,255.06 / 2.68% (FY2026). Total 46,782.88 (FY2026), 38,876.18 (FY2025), 30,148.01 (FY2024). D&B Report: HVAC segment accounts for nearly 65% of total market demand (≈INR 122.3 billion).
internal_operational.title: Product concentration in HVAC components (77.84% of Fiscal 2026 revenue)

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 3. Revenue of ₹46,782.88 lakhs, ₹38,876.18 lakhs and ₹30,148.01 lakhs in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 is derived from white goods (HVAC & Refrigerator), electrical equipment manufacturing, tubing components and fittings, metal manufacturing and others. Demand depends on the end products of OEM customers and is subject to seasonality and cyclicality, which may cause fluctuations in sales volumes, uneven revenue recognition and variations in capacity utilisation across quarters.
internal_operational.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) End-user industry FY2026: White goods (HVAC & Refrigerator) 43,551.89 / 93.09%; Electrical equipment manufacturing 2,505.95 / 5.36%; Tubing components and fitting 192.43 / 0.41%; Metal manufacturing 187.93 / 0.40%; Others 344.67 / 0.74%. Quarter-wise FY2026: Q1 11,391.02 / 24.35%; Q2 7,863.36 / 16.81%; Q3 12,330.92 / 26.36%; Q4 15,197.57 / 32.49%.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on a limited set of end-user industries; seasonality and cyclicality of demand

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 4. Key raw materials are brass scrap, brass honey scrap, copper tubes, steel round bar and consumables such as aluminium solid rod and zinc ingot. Procurement is on a purchase-order basis with no long-term supply contracts; pricing generally follows market prices. Reliance on a select group of suppliers may constrain negotiating ability, and import restrictions, embargoes or higher import duties could adversely affect operations.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on third-party raw material suppliers; supplier concentration and no long-term supply contracts

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 5. As of March 31, 2026 the Company had 762 contractual employees engaged through independent contractors. It may be held responsible for wage payments if contractors default. Non-availability of contract labour, increases in labour cost, adverse regulatory orders, strikes or labour unrest could materially affect operations. No labour disruption was experienced in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
internal_operational.evidence: 762 contractual employees as of March 31, 2026. Contract labour charges (₹ in lakhs): 1,862.03 / 4.18% of total expenses (FY2026), 1,581.10 / 4.36% (FY2025), 1,203.08 / 4.13% (FY2024).
internal_operational.title: Labour-intensive operations and dependence on contract labour

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 6. Customers generally place orders over e-mail against which internal work orders are created; there are no long-term agreements. Production cycles are based on customer demand forecasts. To retain existing customers the Company may be required to offer terms that place restraints on its resources, and it may be reluctant to proceed against customers in disputes.
internal_operational.evidence: Served 61, 52 and 61 customers in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, of which 19 customers were associated with the Company in each of the preceding three Fiscals.
internal_operational.title: No long-term agreements with customers; orders placed over e-mail

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 9. Revenue is derived from customers across 11 states and 1 union territory in India, but on average more than 70% of domestic sales in each of the preceding three Fiscals came from Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Adverse developments in these states — competition, economic conditions, demographic trends, political developments or regulatory changes — could materially affect the business.
internal_operational.evidence: (₹ in lakhs, FY2026 domestic sales) Maharashtra 18,943.87 / 40.49%; Rajasthan 13,722.72 / 29.33%; Uttar Pradesh 6,748.64 / 14.43%; Karnataka 2,505.05 / 5.35%; Haryana 2,155.46 / 4.61%; Gujarat 1,892.24 / 4.04%. FY2025 Uttar Pradesh 11,966.98 / 30.78%. Total domestic sales 46,782.88 (FY2026).
internal_operational.title: Geographic concentration of revenue: more than 70% of domestic sales from three states

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 17. Inventory is planned on the basis of orders received from customers; errors in identifying inventory levels could result in surplus inventory that cannot be sold in a timely manner, or under-stocking that affects the ability to meet customer demand. Over-stocked and unsold inventory may have to be sold at a discount, leading to losses. No such instance occurred in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
internal_operational.title: Inability to accurately forecast customer demand may cause excess inventory or shortages

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 18. Manufacturing requires a steady and abundant supply of power, met through the local state power authority with diesel generators as back-up. Any shortage or disruption in power, fuel or water supply could lead to temporary shutdown of part or all of operations, with additional restart expenses and loss of output. No major interruption occurred in the last three Fiscals.
internal_operational.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Power and fuel expenses 468.87 / 1.05% of total expenses (FY2026), 427.62 / 1.18% (FY2025), 265.20 / 0.91% (FY2024). Total expenses 44,523.91, 36,279.53, 29,164.42.
internal_operational.title: Disruption or shortage of power, fuel or water could halt operations

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 23. The Company operates six manufacturing facilities (two at Noida, Uttar Pradesh and one each at Pune, Maharashtra; Neemrana, Rajasthan; Bengaluru, Karnataka; and Sanand, Gujarat). Capacity utilisation is uneven across lines and years. Installed capacity is computed on stated assumptions (8 hours a day, 25 operational working days, 70% plant capacity for typical cycle time) and certified by an Independent Chartered Engineer; the DRHP states the methodology may not be comparable across the industry and actual utilised capacity may differ significantly.
internal_operational.evidence: Noida Facility 1 sub-total: installed 36,30,000 / utilised 19,85,011 / 54.68% (FY2026) vs 28,50,000 / 17,41,631 / 61.11% (FY2025) and 9,00,000 / 3,15,786 / 35.09% (FY2024). Noida Facility 1 HVAC utilisation fell to 25.59% (FY2026) from 62.48% (FY2025). Noida Facility 2 sub-total 3,36,30,000 / 1,99,22,710 / 59.24% (FY2026) vs 63.90% (FY2025) and 70.37% (FY2024); Refrigerator line 29.82% (FY2026) vs 60.97% and 72.38%. Certificate dated June 29, 2026 from Karan Rajendra Mody (AKV Consulting LLP), Independent Chartered Engineer.
internal_operational.title: Under-utilisation of manufacturing capacity; installed capacity figures rest on assumptions

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 24. Customers, typically OEMs, prescribe specific requirements on sizes, dimensions, configurations and metal grades, and conduct vendor qualification reviews, technical audits and quality inspections. Defects or deviations may result in order cancellations, product rejections or returns, replacement at the Company's own cost, liquidated damages, indemnity or liability claims, product recalls or customer-initiated litigation. No order cancellations, product recalls or material quality-related issues arose during Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
internal_operational.evidence: "While we have not experienced any order cancellations, product recalls or material quality-related issues during the Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, there can be no assurance that such instances will not arise in the future."
internal_operational.title: Requirement to meet precise customer technical specifications and quality standards

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 25. All six manufacturing facilities are located in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Gujarat. Political and regional strikes, labour shortages or strikes, severe weather, natural disasters, epidemics, floods and lengthy power outages in these states could disrupt manufacturing and cause delivery delays. Changes in government policies in these states, including increased taxes or duties, may require a change in business strategy.
internal_operational.evidence: Six (6) manufacturing facilities: two in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, and one each in Pune, Maharashtra; Neemrana, Rajasthan; Bengaluru, Karnataka; and Sanand, Gujarat. No material disruptions at the facilities in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
internal_operational.title: Manufacturing operations concentrated in five states

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 29. Operations involve cutting, bending and drilling performed under potentially dangerous circumstances. Hazards listed include explosions, fires, mechanical failures and other operational problems, discharges or releases of hazardous substances, chemicals or gases, and other environmental risks. An accident could cause serious injury or death, property damage, suspension of operations or imposition of civil or criminal liabilities, and could give rise to occupational-exposure claims. An occupational health and safety policy and fire safety systems have been adopted.
internal_operational.evidence: "However, there have been no such instances have occurred in last three Fiscals which may have an adverse impact on the business and financial operations of our Company."
internal_operational.title: Hazardous working conditions in manufacturing operations

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 32. The Company is led by Promoters Jignesh Panchal, Dina Panchal, Jugal Jignesh Panchal and Jubin Jignesh Panchal with cumulative experience of more than four decades, and Whole-time Director and CFO Navneet Bhardwaj with more than 20 years in the tubular component industry. Loss of senior executives or key employees could disrupt operations; competition for skilled personnel is intense and may require faster increases in employee compensation.
internal_operational.evidence: Attrition rate 49.53% (as of March 31, 2026), 36.34% (2025), 45.73% (2024). Employees at end of period 393, 350, 327; additions 227, 146, 175; deletions 184, 123, 142.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on Promoters, Key Managerial Personnel and skilled personnel; high employee attrition

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 34. Policies cover manufacturing facilities, buildings, plant and machinery, furniture, fixtures and fittings and stocks against fire, burglary, earthquake and other perils, plus public liability, marine/inland transit, group accidental and group mediclaim and vehicle cover. Policies carry standard limitations on interruption length and maximum claim; uninsured losses, third-party claims exceeding limits, economic or consequential damages and excluded claims may not be covered, and policies may not be renewable on commercially acceptable terms.
internal_operational.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Insurable assets 11,621.98 (FY2026), 9,184.39 (FY2025), 8,210.65 (FY2024). Total insurance coverage 35,400.20, 24,422.58, 20,690.65. Insurable assets as a percentage of total insurance coverage: 304.60, 265.91, 252.00.
internal_operational.title: Insurance coverage may not be adequate to cover all potential losses

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 40. Transportation of raw materials into the manufacturing facilities and of finished products to customers uses third-party fleets. Disruption in these services or transportation strikes could impair delivery; freight cost increases that cannot be passed through would lower margins. There is also exposure to theft, accidents and loss of products in transit, for which insurance may not be sufficient. No significant disruptions occurred in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
internal_operational.evidence: (₹ in lakhs) Carriage inward and outward expenses 695.31 / 1.56% of total expenses (FY2026), 837.78 / 2.31% (FY2025), 653.80 / 2.24% (FY2024).
internal_operational.title: Dependence on third-party transportation and logistics providers; risk of theft, accident or loss in transit

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 41. Premises including the Registered Office and the manufacturing facilities are on leasehold land or taken on lease / leave and licence. Failure to comply with conditions of use, or inability to extend or renew on commercially reasonable terms, could force relocation and result in relocation expenses. Lease/rental payments may increase and lock-in periods may limit the ability to exit. No lessor is a related party and there were no instances of material breach or dispute during Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
internal_operational.evidence: Noida Facility-1 and Registered Office — lease from U. P. State Industrial Development Corporation Limited for 90 years from September 01, 2000 and September 23, 2000. Noida Facility-2 — 90 years from January 12, 2011. Pune Facility — leave and licence from M/s. S. G. Industries for two (2) years from December 1, 2025. Warehouse (Satara) — leave and licence from M/s. Om Sai Industries for thirty-three (33) months from December 01, 2024. Vacant land, Ranjangaon — MIDC lease for 95 years from March 3, 2025. Bengaluru Facility — two leases of sixty (60) months each from January 1, 2025 (Mr. Eerappa; Mr. Ramaiah). Sanand Facility — GIDC leases of 99 years from November 8, 2011 and February 23, 2018. Neemrana Facility — RIICO lease of 99 years from November 01, 2021.
internal_operational.title: Registered Office and manufacturing facilities held on leasehold land or leave-and-licence basis

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 46. The Company uses Sofgen (ERP for finance, inventory, material management, procurement and sales), MMC software (payroll and employee records), Solid Work (design of tools, jigs and fixtures) and WebTel for TDS returns, supported by an in-house IT team and third-party services. These systems may be vulnerable to outages from fire, floods, power loss, telecommunications failures, natural disasters, computer viruses, cyber threats or malware and break-ins.
internal_operational.evidence: "However, we have not faced any such instances in the Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024."
internal_operational.title: Exposure to malfunction or disruption of information technology systems

internal_operational.detail: Risk factor 54 (External Risk Factors). Cyclones, storms, floods, earthquakes, tsunamis, tornadoes, fires, explosions, pandemics and man-made disasters including acts of terrorism and military actions could adversely affect results of operations, cash flows or financial condition. Deterioration in international relations, especially between India and neighbouring countries, and local civil disturbances could also affect the price of the Equity Shares.
internal_operational.evidence: "The occurrence of natural disasters, including cyclones, storms, floods, earthquakes, tsunamis, tornadoes, fires, explosions, pandemic and man-made disasters, including acts of terrorism and military actions, could adversely affect our results of operations, cash flows or financial condition."
internal_operational.title: Natural or man-made disasters, hostilities, terrorist attacks and civil unrest

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 10. Products are marketed and sold mainly in India and the Company plans to expand its presence. Expansion may require significant management attention and financial resources. Listed inherent risks include uncertainties in cooperation with new business associates including traders, logistics and transportation providers; increased marketing costs in new regions; entry barriers and difficulties in establishing brand recognition; exposure to expropriation or other government actions; the burden of complying with a variety of foreign laws including delays in obtaining approvals, permits and import/export licences; inability to adapt to consumer preferences and local trends; longer accounts receivable collection periods; credit risk and higher levels of payment fraud; increases in transportation costs; uncertainty regarding liability for supply of low-quality products; and actions by foreign governments under trade or other restrictions.
strategy_growth.evidence: Eleven enumerated risks (i)-(xi) listed in the risk factor, including "longer accounts receivable collection periods and greater difficulty in accounts receivable collection due to lower bargaining power in a less familiar market".
strategy_growth.title: Expansion of the customer base into new markets subjects the Company to business, economic, political, regulatory and legal risks

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 15. Net Proceeds are to fund (i) capital expenditure for proposed expansion of the Sanand Facility, Gujarat; (ii) setting up a new manufacturing facility at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh; (iii) repayment or prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings; and (iv) general corporate purposes. Estimation relies on the Techno Economic Viability Report by CARE Analytics and Advisory Private Limited dated July 3, 2026. No orders have been placed for plant or machinery for the Sri City Facility or the Sanand expansion as of the date of the DRHP, and no definitive agreements have been entered into with third parties; quotations are valid only for limited periods and may be revised. Actual costs may exceed the quoted amounts, and the Company may ultimately contract with different vendors.
strategy_growth.evidence: ₹6,318.36 lakhs from the Net Proceeds for capital expenditure, comprising ₹4,268.60 lakhs for the proposed expansion of the Sanand Facility at Sanand, Gujarat and ₹2,049.76 lakhs for setting up a new manufacturing facility at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh. TEV Report by CARE Analytics and Advisory Private Limited (formerly Care Risk Solutions Private Limited) dated July 3, 2026.
strategy_growth.title: ₹6,318.36 lakhs of Net Proceeds earmarked for capex based on third-party quotations; project not appraised by any bank or financial institution

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 16. At Sanand the Company proposes to manufacture air conditioner service valves (2-way and 3-way) using brass; at Sri City it proposes to set up an AC copper tubing assembly line with a proposed production capacity of 6,000 sets per day. Weak market demand, labour disruptions, foreign exchange rate fluctuations and failure to receive approvals from government and statutory authorities could cause delay or non-completion. Expansion or setting up a facility is subject to government supervision and approval procedures including project approvals and filings, construction land and project planning approvals, environment protection approvals, pollution discharge permits, factory and labour licences, work safety approvals and fire protection approvals.
strategy_growth.evidence: Sri City Facility proposed production capacity of 6,000 sets per day of AC Copper Tubing Assembly. "While we have not experienced any such delays in the procurement requisite business approvals for expansion of any of our manufacturing facilities in the Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, any such delays could result in us becoming subject to administrative uncertainty, fines, or the suspension of use of such projects."
strategy_growth.title: Delays, disruptions or cost overruns in the Sanand expansion and the new Sri City facility

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 21. The planned use of Net Proceeds is based on current conditions and management estimates and has not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or other independent party. Under Sections 13(8) and 27 of the Companies Act, 2013 no variation may be undertaken without a special resolution of shareholders. Approval may not be obtained in a timely manner or at all, and the Promoters would be required to provide an exit opportunity to shareholders who do not agree to the proposed variation.
strategy_growth.evidence: "we cannot undertake any variation in the utilisation of the Net Proceeds as disclosed in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus without obtaining the approval of shareholders of our Company through a special resolution."
strategy_growth.title: Variation in the utilisation of Net Proceeds requires prior shareholder approval by special resolution

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 22. Funding requirements are based on management estimates, current business circumstances, prevailing market conditions and other commercial and technical factors and have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution. They are subject to change in light of financial condition, business strategy and external factors such as government policies, market conditions, competitive environment and interest or exchange rate fluctuations. Deployment of the Gross Proceeds will be monitored by a monitoring agency appointed pursuant to the SEBI ICDR Regulations. Internal management estimates may exceed fair market value, requiring rescheduling or reallocation of expenditure.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Accordingly, prospective investors in the Offer will need to rely upon our management's judgment with respect to the use of Net Proceeds."
strategy_growth.title: Funding requirements and deployment of Net Proceeds based on management estimates, not appraised by any bank

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 26. The growth strategy involves expanding the customer base, establishing market position in the tubing components industry in India, enhancing the geographical footprint of manufacturing operations, capitalising on market opportunity, and enhancing productivity and operational efficiencies through both organic and inorganic growth. Enumerated risks include delays and cost overruns from unavailability of timely supplies of raw material, equipment and technologies; inability to hire, train and retain skilled sales and marketing personnel; inability to develop and maintain supplier and customer relationships; delays or denial of required government approvals; diversion of management attention; competition including from companies in other countries supplying copper tubes, aluminium coils, SS fittings and brass connectors at lower prices due to scale efficiencies and subsidised ecosystems; anti-dumping duties and lower cost of imports; changes in government policies and initiatives; failure of customers and suppliers to adhere to specifications and timelines; failure to maintain high quality control standards; shortage of raw materials; and failure to execute expansion plans effectively.
strategy_growth.evidence: "If the expenditure that we will incur on the setting up of new manufacturing facility or proposed expansion does not produce anticipated or desired results, our profitability, cash flows and financial condition will be adversely affected."
strategy_growth.title: Execution risk in growth strategies

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 28. The Company seeks to improve technological capability and operational efficiency through modernisation of manufacturing lines or replacement of equipment, enhancements in manufacturing methods, material handling, inventory control, quality assurance and software integration. Failure to keep pace with evolving technologies, upgrade equipment in line with market expectations, adopt automation or invest in research and development could increase production costs, cause operational inefficiencies or an inability to meet customer demand, and undermine competitive position.
strategy_growth.evidence: "our cost of processing may increase relative to our competitors, which may have an adverse impact on our business, results of operations, and financial condition."
strategy_growth.title: Risk of technology and equipment obsolescence without continued investment

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 31. The Company faces competition from companies operating in the tubing components and fittings industry in India, and pricing pressure from domestic companies able to manufacture HVAC, refrigerator, brass and VRV components at competitive costs and supply at cheaper prices. Entry of new competitors and consolidation of existing ones could intensify the competitive landscape.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Our key competitors include KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration Limited and The Anup Engineering Limited. (Source: D&B Report)"
strategy_growth.title: Competition from domestic companies in the tubing components and fittings industry

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 44. Dun and Bradstreet was appointed pursuant to an engagement letter dated November 27, 2025 to prepare the "Industry Report on Tubing Components and Fittings Industry" dated July 3, 2026, commissioned and paid for by the Company. The report uses certain methodologies for market sizing and forecasting and may include numbers relating to the Company that differ from those recorded internally; disclosures are limited to excerpts and the report has not been reproduced in its entirety. Dun and Bradstreet is stated to have no relationship with the Company, Promoters, Directors, Promoter Group members, Key Managerial Personnel, Senior Management Personnel or the Book Running Lead Manager as of the date of the DRHP.
strategy_growth.evidence: Engagement letter dated November 27, 2025; D&B Report dated July 3, 2026. "Industry sources and publications may also base their information on estimates, projections, forecasts and assumptions that may prove to be incorrect."
strategy_growth.title: Industry disclosure derived from a commissioned D&B Report

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 53 (External Risk Factors). Any slowdown in the growth of the Indian economy or future volatility in global commodity prices could adversely affect business, financial condition and results of operations. The Indian economy could be affected by a general rise in interest rates, currency fluctuations, adverse conditions affecting housing and tourism and electricity prices. Financial turmoil in the United States, Europe, China or Asian emerging markets may affect the Indian economy, and a loss of investor confidence in emerging market financial systems may cause increased volatility in Indian financial markets.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Any slowdown in the growth of the Indian economy or any future volatility in global commodity prices could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations."
strategy_growth.title: Slowdown in economic growth in India

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 57 (External Risk Factors). The DRHP cites the ongoing military conflicts between Russia and Ukraine in Europe and the Israel-Iran conflict in the Middle East, the possibility of default in the US debt market, concerns over a trade war between large economies, and rising concerns of a slowdown in the Chinese economy alongside a strained India-China relationship. These could increase volatility in global and Indian markets, reduce global market liquidity and restrict access to capital.
strategy_growth.evidence: "In particular, the ongoing military conflicts between Russia and Ukraine in Europe, Israel and Iran conflict in the Middle East could result in increased volatility in, or damage to, the worldwide financial markets and economy."
strategy_growth.title: Financial and political instability in other countries may increase volatility in Indian financial markets

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 58 (External Risk Factors). Increases in global crude oil prices may raise costs of transportation, logistics, energy, packaging and certain raw materials, adversely affecting operating margins where increased costs cannot be passed on in a timely manner. Geopolitical conflicts, trade restrictions, sanctions or regional instability may disrupt supply chains, increase freight and insurance costs, delay procurement of raw materials, components and consumables, reduce order volumes and lower capacity utilisation, and may increase borrowing costs and tighten liquidity.
strategy_growth.evidence: The DRHP cites "developments involving Israel, United States of America and Iran and concerns relating to the security of key maritime transport routes such as the Strait of Hormuz".
strategy_growth.title: Increases in crude oil prices and geopolitical or war-like conditions

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 60 (External Risk Factors). The performance and growth of the business depend on the performance of the Indian economy, which has been affected by global economic uncertainties and liquidity crises, domestic policy and the political environment, volatility in interest rates, currency exchange rates, commodity and electricity prices, adverse conditions affecting agriculture and rising inflation. Risk management initiatives by banks and lenders could affect the availability of funds or lead to withdrawal of existing credit facilities. An increase in the trade deficit, a downgrade in India's sovereign debt rating or a decline in foreign exchange reserves could negatively affect interest rates and liquidity.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Any downturn in the macroeconomic environment in India could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operation and the trading price of our Equity Shares."
strategy_growth.title: Revenue derived from operations in India; decline in economic growth or political instability

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 61 (External Risk Factors). Enumerated factors that may adversely affect the Indian economy include exchange rate fluctuations and currency controls; scarcity of credit or other financing in India; prevailing income conditions among Indian customers and corporations; geo-political issues; tariff related measures, anti-dumping and other trade and tariff protections on raw materials or manufactured products; epidemics or other public health events; macroeconomic factors and central bank regulation including interest rate movements; volatility in trading activity on India's principal stock exchanges; decline in India's foreign exchange reserves; downgrading of India's sovereign debt rating; and difficulty in developing partnerships with local businesses.
strategy_growth.evidence: "For example, our manufacturing facilities are located in western India, hence any significant disruption, including due to social, political or economic factors or natural calamities or civil disruptions, impacting this region may adversely affect our operations."
strategy_growth.title: Regulatory, economic, social and political uncertainties beyond the Company's control

strategy_growth.detail: Risk factor 62 (External Risk Factors). Inflation rates in India have been volatile and India has experienced high inflation in the recent past. Increased inflation can contribute to higher interest rates and increased costs including salaries and other expenses. High fluctuations may make it more difficult to accurately estimate or control costs, and increases may not be passable to customers in whole or in part.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Further, the GoI has previously initiated economic measures to combat high inflation rates, and it is unclear whether these measures will remain in effect."
strategy_growth.title: Inflation in India may not be passable to customers at a proportional rate

concerns_observed: Profit fell while revenue grew: PAT declined to Rs 1,755.59 lakhs (FY2026) from Rs 2,048.31 lakhs (FY2025) though revenue from operations rose 20.31% to Rs 46,808.59 lakhs; EPS fell from Rs 13.51 to Rs 11.12 and RoNW from 26.35% to 18.61%, while stated EBITDA barely moved (Rs 3,923.01 lakhs to Rs 3,979.14 lakhs) against depreciation up from Rs 832.10 lakhs to Rs 1,049.96 lakhs and finance cost from Rs 603.17 lakhs to Rs 757.79 lakhs.

Utilisation is falling as capacity is added, before the Objects add more: grand-total installed capacity 3,83,43,000 to 5,39,40,000 to 6,91,20,000 Nos with utilisation 66.03% to 61.03% to 58.67%; Noida Facility 1's HVAC line fell to 25.59% (from 62.48%), Noida Facility 2's refrigerator line to 29.82% (from 72.38% in FY2024), and Bengaluru's installed capacity was actually cut from 15,60,000 to 9,60,000 Nos with utilisation at 47.34%.

Demand rests on 61 customers with nothing contractual behind it: top 5 at 84.09% and top 10 at 96.60% of FY2026 revenue, both higher than FY2024's 75.45% and 92.01%; Risk Factor 6 states customers place orders over e-mail with no long-term agreements, and only 19 customers were associated with the Company in each of the three preceding Fiscals.

Cash generation is going backwards as the business scales: CFO fell from Rs 1,671.93 lakhs (FY2024) to Rs 1,206.62 lakhs (FY2025) to Rs 1,156.84 lakhs (FY2026) while revenue rose from Rs 30,170.42 lakhs to Rs 46,808.59 lakhs; CFO was below PAT of Rs 1,755.59 lakhs in FY2026, CFI was negative in all three years (Rs 2,716.85, Rs 2,705.56 and Rs 1,825.44 lakhs) and CFF positive in all three (Rs 1,568.72, Rs 1,516.16 and Rs 18.57 lakhs) - growth has been debt-funded.

The balance sheet is already stretched before the expansion: total borrowings rose Rs 5,014.62 to Rs 7,033.61 to Rs 9,654.71 lakhs (debt-to-equity 0.91, 0.90 and 1.02 times), net working capital of Rs 9,799.24 lakhs (20.93% of revenue, up from 17.03% in FY2024) exceeds net worth of Rs 9,434.35 lakhs, and cash and cash equivalents at March 31, 2026 were Rs 44.77 lakhs.

Concentration is increasing, not diversifying: white goods (HVAC and refrigerator) rose to 93.09% of FY2026 revenue from 88.11% in FY2024, HVAC components alone are 77.84% of revenue, and Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh together are 84.25% of FY2026 domestic sales - with Uttar Pradesh collapsing from 30.78% (FY2025) to 14.43% (FY2026) while Rajasthan went 16.22% to 29.33%.

Attrition is running at roughly half the workforce a year: 49.53% as of March 31, 2026, 36.34% (2025) and 45.73% (2024), on a permanent headcount of 393, 350 and 327 (227 additions against 184 deletions in FY2026), alongside 762 contractual employees engaged through independent contractors at contract labour charges of Rs 1,862.03 lakhs.

Both Objects step outside what the Company has demonstrated: Sanand is a new product (2-way and 3-way air conditioner service valves, 16,000 sets per day, board-approved July 10, 2026) and Sri City is a new state (6,000 sets per day of AC copper tubing assembly), against a Company whose Sanand site itself is still awaiting its consolidated consent and authorisation.

Cash left the Company for the promoter family in a year of rising debt: Jignesh Panchal took Rs 72.00 lakhs remuneration, Rs 105.67 lakhs dividend and Rs 26.34 lakhs of interest on his unsecured loan in FY2026 (against Rs 60.00 lakhs and Rs 60.39 lakhs in FY2025), while total borrowings rose to Rs 9,654.71 lakhs and closing cash was Rs 44.77 lakhs.

The senior layer is new and untested at a listed company: all four Independent Directors (Abhishek Mahay, Ajay Kumar Trivedi, Shashank Nareshchandra Sheth, Nancy Verma) were appointed on the single date January 24, 2026; the CFO seat changed twice in six months, with Rohit Kumar Tiwary appointed with effect from January 1, 2026 (Rs 15.13 lakhs FY2026 remuneration) and Navneet Bhardwaj appointed Chief Financial Officer on June 15, 2026; Risk Factor 52 states none of the Directors has been on the board of a listed company.

Input side is concentrated, uncontracted and dominant in the cost base: cost of goods sold was 82.84% of total expenses in FY2026 (Rs 36,881.53 lakhs of Rs 44,523.91 lakhs), top 5 suppliers were 54.43% and top 10 were 71.75% of purchases, and Risk Factor 4 states there are no long-term supply contracts, with pricing following market prices on a purchase-order basis.

Revenue is back-loaded within the year: Q4 was 32.49%, 36.12% and 36.23% of revenue from operations in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024 against Q2 at 16.81%, 17.51% and 15.45%, and the DRHP itself states this may adversely impact cash flows, working capital and inventory management.
data_gaps: No price band exists at this DRHP stage. The Fresh Issue amount, Offer for Sale amount, Gross Proceeds, Offer expenses, Net Proceeds, general corporate purposes amount, the Total of the Utilisation of Net Proceeds table, post-Offer share capital, dilution percentage and post-Offer promoter percentage all print [.] - so no valuation, market capitalisation or P/E can be stated, and the peer average P/E of 71.01 (Anup 41.97, KRN 100.04, on NSE closing prices of July 06, 2026) has nothing on this side to compare against.

EBITDA margin, PAT margin, RoCE and RoE are not carried in the routed financial data - every field is null for all three years. Only RoNW is stated (18.61% / 26.35% / 15.63%), so profitability trend work here rests on the absolute EBITDA and PAT figures rather than on margins printed by the issuer.

The stated EBITDA of Rs 3,979.14 / 3,923.01 / 2,056.37 lakhs cannot be reconciled from the extracted evidence. The 'Non-GAAP Financial Measures' section at page 358, which would contain the reconciliation, was not routed to this pipeline.

The receivables ageing that was routed is dated March 31, 2024, not FY2026: Rs 33.25 lakhs beyond one year, 0.35% of net worth. The FY2026 ageing schedule was not routed, so the Rs 7,004.69 lakhs of trade receivables at March 31, 2026 cannot be aged and that 0.35% figure must not be paired with FY2026 net worth.

Per-facility interest rates are not disclosed for any of the twenty borrowings. Only a portfolio band of 7.00% to 9.00% per annum is given, with the HSBC and Citi Bank N.A. facilities flagged benchmark-linked and floating; only the ICICI vehicle loan (8.80%) and the promoter unsecured loan (8.00%) carry stated rates.

Inventory days, creditor days and the cash conversion cycle are null in the working capital data; inventory days of 60 / 61 / 72 appear only inside a risk factor's evidence and no creditor-days or cycle figure is printed anywhere in the routed extract.

Post-expansion capacity cannot be totalled. The Objects add 16,000 sets per day at Sanand and 6,000 sets per day at Sri City, which are not commensurable with the existing 6,91,20,000 Nos per annum base, and the DRHP prints no combined post-expansion capacity figure.

The board committee table was not reproduced in the routed extract, so committee names, memberships and chairmanships cannot be verified - only the Company's own statement that it complies with SEBI Listing Regulations and Companies Act composition norms.
