open_questions: Why did PAT fall to Rs 1,755.59 lakhs in FY2026 from Rs 2,048.31 lakhs on 20.31% higher revenue, and how much of that fall is the FY2025-versus-FY2026 consolidated-to-standalone basis change (the removal of Sai Ganesh Exports Private Limited) as against genuine margin compression, given depreciation rose Rs 832.10 to 1,049.96 lakhs and finance cost Rs 603.17 to 757.79 lakhs?

Why does stated EBITDA of Rs 3,979.14 / 3,923.01 / 2,056.37 lakhs not reproduce from the restated profit and loss under the DRHP's own formula, which yields Rs 4,092.43 / 4,063.53 / 2,156.93 lakhs, and what is the reconciling item disclosed at page 358 that the routed extract does not carry?

Grand-total utilisation fell 66.03% to 61.03% to 58.67% while installed capacity nearly doubled, Noida Facility 1's HVAC line fell to 25.59% and Noida Facility 2's refrigerator line to 29.82%. On what demand evidence are a further 16,000 sets/day at Sanand and 6,000 sets/day at Sri City justified, and why was Bengaluru's installed capacity cut from 15,60,000 to 9,60,000 Nos?

Every machinery quotation for both Objects expires before the scheduled ordering date - Sanand validities of 30/08/2026 to 29/10/2026 against ordering from March 2027, Sri City validities of 26/09/2026 to 28/12/2026 against procurement from December 2026. What re-quotation, escalation or vendor-substitution protection exists, given no contingency line is printed and escalation is to be met from unquantified internal accruals? Will any order be placed before the Prospectus?

Why does the HSBC working capital facility show an outstanding of Rs 4,313.79 lakhs against a sanction of Rs 4,300.00 lakhs at March 31, 2026, what is the actual rate on that facility within the disclosed 7.00% to 9.00% portfolio band, and what interest saving does the Rs 3,500.00 lakhs repayment produce against the FY2026 finance cost of Rs 757.79 lakhs?

Sanand's consolidated consent and authorisation, Noida Facility 2's consent to operate, the Bengaluru fire advisory and the Neemrana contract labour registration are all applied for and not received. When were the applications filed, what is the expected date of grant, and on what legal basis do Noida Facility 2 (3,36,30,000 Nos of installed capacity) and Sanand continue to operate in the meantime?

The Sri City project has eight of nine approvals outstanding, with the DRHP's own note conceding the process 'is currently at an early stage'. How does building and civil works commencing December 2026 sit with a consent to establish that is required before commencement of construction, and what slippage would push commercial operation past March 2028?

Under the Design Rights Agreements dated May 27, 2026, the 'Six axis multi location linear movement brazing machine' designs registered in India and the UK remain owned by Jignesh Panchal and Dina Panchal and are licensed to the Company for ten years, 'renewable as mutually agreed'. Why were the designs and the four jointly-filed patent applications not assigned outright to the Company before listing, and what happens at renewal?

Permanent-employee attrition ran 45.73%, 36.34% and 49.53% across the three Fiscals on a base of about 350 people, alongside 762 contract workers. What drives it, is it concentrated at a particular facility or grade, and what does it imply for staffing two new plants that are meant to run automated lines?

The Chief Financial Officer changed twice within six months - Rohit Kumar Tiwary with effect from January 1, 2026 and Navneet Bhardwaj on June 15, 2026, the latter also a Whole-time Director and previously Senior Accountant at the amalgamated Sai Ganesh Exports. What were the circumstances of the change, and how is independence of the finance function preserved when the CFO is also an executive Director?

Section 123(4) was breached in four separate Fiscals (2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025) and Form CHG-1 was never filed for the ICICI vehicle loan. What remediation and compliance framework has been put in place, and what penalty exposure attaches to the pending Section 454 adjudication and to Section 86?

Daikin, LG and Haier together are 64.87% of FY2026 revenue with no long-term agreements and orders placed by e-mail. What is the vendor-qualification status and share-of-wallet at each, and would the new Sanand service-valve line and the Sri City assembly line be qualified with those same three customers or sold to a different set?
verdict.our_read: A 99.99% promoter-held (seven shareholders in total) contract manufacturer of copper and brass HVAC, VRV and refrigerator tubing for white-goods OEMs - 93.09% of FY2026 revenue from one end-industry, 84.09% from five customers and 33.40% from Daikin alone - whose make-or-break tension is that it is asking for Rs 6,318.36 lakhs to build wholly un-ordered new capacity at Sanand and Sri City while the existing 6,91,20,000 Nos base ran at 58.67% utilisation, down from 66.03% in Fiscal 2024, and FY2026 PAT fell to Rs 1,755.59 lakhs from Rs 2,048.31 lakhs on 20.31% higher revenue.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue from operations Rs 30,170.42 to 38,907.79 to 46,808.59 lakhs (CAGR 24.58%) but PAT went Rs 857.07 to 2,048.31 to 1,755.59 lakhs, EPS Rs 5.68 to 13.51 to 11.12 and RoNW 15.63% to 26.35% to 18.61% - the latest year is down on all three despite 20.31% revenue growth. Marked down further because FY2025 is consolidated while FY2024 and FY2026 are standalone, so the peak year is not on the same basis as the year it is compared against.

CFO fell Rs 1,671.93 to 1,206.62 to 1,156.84 lakhs while revenue rose 55%; FY2026 CFO is below PAT of Rs 1,755.59 lakhs. Borrowings rose Rs 5,014.62 to 7,033.61 to 9,654.71 lakhs (debt-to-equity 1.02x), cash at March 31, 2026 is Rs 44.77 lakhs, and net working capital of Rs 9,799.24 lakhs exceeds net worth of Rs 9,434.35 lakhs. CFF was positive in all three years, so the capex of Rs 2,693.77 / 2,437.48 / 1,574.64 lakhs has been funded by debt, not operations.

No order book or unexecuted order value appears anywhere in the routed data; Risk Factor 6 states customers place orders by e-mail with no long-term agreements. Visibility rests on 61 customers of which only 19 recur across all three Fiscals, with top 5 at 84.09% and Daikin alone at 33.40%. Against that, grand-total utilisation fell 66.03% to 61.03% to 58.67% - the Company is producing into less of what it already has.

Every line of the Rs 6,318.36 lakhs capex rests on a quotation, with the notes stating no definitive vendor agreements exist, contradicting the chapter's claim of support by purchase orders; validities of 30/08/2026 to 29/10/2026 (Sanand) and 26/09/2026 to 28/12/2026 (Sri City) all lapse before the scheduled ordering dates of March 2027 and December 2026. No bank or FI appraisal, only a Company-commissioned CARE TEV report dated July 3, 2026. The Rs 3,500.00 lakhs repayment targets an HSBC facility whose Rs 4,313.79 lakhs outstanding exceeds its Rs 4,300.00 lakhs sanction, at an undisclosed per-facility rate. General corporate purposes and the utilisation Total both print [.].
parameter_scores.parameter: Use of Offer proceeds - quality and commitment

parameter_scores.basis: Sanand adds 16,000 sets/day of a product the Company has never made (2-way and 3-way AC service valves) and Sri City adds 6,000 sets/day in a new state, on top of a base running at 58.67% and falling. Sanand's consolidated consent and authorisation and consent to operate are both outstanding; eight of Sri City's nine approvals are 'Yet to be received' with the DRHP noting the process is 'at an early stage'. Both projects target commercial operation in Fiscal 2028 (April 2028 and March 2028) with civil works starting December 2026.

Installed capacity was raised 3,83,43,000 to 5,39,40,000 to 6,91,20,000 Nos while utilisation fell 66.03% to 61.03% to 58.67%. Noida Facility 1's HVAC line dropped to 25.59% from 62.48%, Noida Facility 2's refrigerator line to 29.82% from 72.38% (FY2024), and Bengaluru's installed capacity was cut from 15,60,000 to 9,60,000 Nos at 47.34% utilisation. Only the brass line (0.26% to 59.88% to 71.76%) and VRV (73.79%) show capacity being filled after it was added.

Section 123(4) dividend-account breaches in four Fiscals (2021, 2022, 2024, 2025) with a Section 454 adjudication application pending; CHG-1 never filed for the ICICI vehicle loan (Section 77); delayed filings across seven form types; statutory dues delayed in all three years. Four consents applied for and not received including consent to operate for the largest facility. Stated EBITDA does not reproduce under the DRHP's own formula in any of the three years. Credit for four Independent Directors of eight, two women Directors, nil promoter pledge and NIL litigation against Promoters, Directors and KMPs.

Aggregate related-party transactions are small - Rs 302.83 / 235.61 / 290.40 lakhs, or 0.65% / 0.61% / 0.96% of revenue from operations - and 46 rows across 14 counterparties are mostly promoter-family remuneration, dividend and sitting fees. Trading with Jaepan Manufacturing Co. (Proprietorship) and Jaepan Manufacturing Company (Partnership Firm) is immaterial (FY2026 purchases Rs 14.08 and Rs 0.56 lakhs; sales Rs 8.80 and Rs 5.76 lakhs). Held back by Rs 341.32 lakhs of promoter unsecured loan repayable on demand at 8.00%, Rs 26.34 lakhs of interest paid on it in FY2026, and Note 32(G) printing no sub-totals for any block.

Promoters hold 99.99% with nil pledge and have given personal guarantees on the secured borrowings; the Offer for Sale is small at up to 2,60,000 shares against a Fresh Issue of up to 49,20,000. But the register is seven shareholders (three public holders own 30 shares between them), Jignesh Panchal's average cost of acquisition is Rs 0.69 per share against Rs 43.65 for Dina Panchal, Rs 40.00 for Jugal and Rs 26.75 for Jubin, and the weighted average cost of all shares transacted is Rs 2.36 over three years against Rs 43.64 over eighteen months. Post-Offer promoter percentage, dilution and the entire lock-in table print [.].

No market share is stated for the Company; FY2026 revenue of INR 468.09 crore is 2.31% of the INR 202.2 billion Indian tubing components and fittings market sized by the commissioned D&B Report. The Company follows a quarterly pricing model on both procurement and sales with cost of goods sold at 82.84% of total expenses, and Risk Factor 31 names domestic competitors able to supply at cheaper prices. Offsetting: ISO 9001/14001/45001 across facilities, ZED Gold at Noida Facility 2, and RoNW of 18.61% above both named listed peers.

Top 5 customers 84.09% and top 10 96.60% of FY2026 revenue (up from 75.45% and 92.01% in FY2024) across only 61 customers, with Daikin at 33.40%, LG at 16.78% and Haier at 14.69% and no long-term agreements. White goods is 93.09% of revenue and HVAC components 77.84%; Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh are 84.25% of FY2026 domestic sales. On the input side, top 5 suppliers are 54.43% of purchases, also uncontracted.

Against the Company: one tax proceeding of Rs 137.58 lakhs, being a demand for excess ITC availed in GSTR3B/GSTR9 not confirmed in GSTR2B/2A for FY 2023-24 - equal to 1.46% of net worth against a materiality threshold of Rs 77.68 lakhs adopted May 22, 2026. By the Company: one Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act complaint (38628 of 2021) for Rs 2.27 lakhs plus 18% interest. NIL both by and against Directors other than Promoters, Promoters, KMPs and Senior Management. A prior income tax demand of Rs 50.12 lakhs (AY 2009-10) now stands NIL after a Section 154 application. Marked down only for the pending Section 454 adjudication and the unfiled CHG-1.

Attrition of 49.53%, 36.34% and 45.73% on 393, 350 and 327 permanent employees. The CFO chair moved twice in six months - Rohit Kumar Tiwary with effect from January 1, 2026, then Navneet Bhardwaj appointed June 15, 2026 - and the Company Secretary joined April 28, 2025. All four Independent Directors were appointed January 24, 2026 and Risk Factor 52 states none of the Directors has listed-company board experience. Four of eight Directors are promoter family, including a 26-year-old Whole-time Director with 'over two (2) years' of industry experience. Only one KMP is populated in the routed data.

red_flags: Not one rupee of the Rs 6,318.36 lakhs capital-expenditure object has been ordered, and the chapter contradicts itself on that point. The DRHP states cost estimates are supported by purchase orders and vendor quotations, yet every annexure line at both Sanand (Rs 4,268.60 lakhs) and Sri City (Rs 2,049.76 lakhs) is footnoted 'As per the quotation received from Suppliers' and the notes to both Objects state: 'we have not entered into any definitive agreements with any of the vendor and there can be no assurance that the same vendor would be engaged to eventually supply the Machinery or other works at the same costs.' Worse, the quotations expire before the Company plans to order: Sanand machinery quotations carry validity of 30/08/2026 to 29/10/2026 while 'Order of Plant & Machineries' is scheduled to commence in March 2027, and Sri City quotations expire 26/09/2026 to 28/12/2026 against procurement commencing December 2026. The project has not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency - the only third-party work is a Techno Economic Viability Report by CARE Analytics and Advisory Private Limited dated July 3, 2026, and any escalation is to be met from internal accruals that are nowhere quantified.

Facilities that are already running do not have their environmental consents in hand, including the largest one. Risk Factor 33 discloses four approvals applied for but not received: consent to operate for Noida Facility 2 - which carries 3,36,30,000 Nos of the 6,91,20,000 Nos total installed capacity - the consolidated consent and authorisation for the Sanand Facility, which is the very site of the Rs 4,268.60 lakhs expansion, the fire advisory for the Bengaluru Facility, and the contract labour registration for the Neemrana Facility, where the Company employs part of its 762 contract workforce. Risk Factor 33 is graded high and the DRHP concedes that violations can result in suspension, revocation or non-renewal of permits or closure of facilities.

Sanction and outstanding do not agree on the single facility the repayment object targets. The Rs 3,500.00 lakhs repayment Object is applied to one loan: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited working capital facility, first sanctioned January 17, 2019, sanctioned amount Rs 4,300.00 lakhs, amount outstanding Rs 4,313.79 lakhs as on March 31, 2026 - an outstanding above the sanction, on a facility whose tenure is stated as 'Payable on Demand'. No per-facility interest rate is disclosed anywhere; the loan table gives only a portfolio band of 7.00% to 9.00% per annum tied to MCLR, 3M T-bill or another bank-chosen benchmark, and both the HSBC and Citi Bank N.A. lines are flagged floating, so the interest saving from the repayment cannot be computed from this document.

Statutory non-compliance is repeated rather than isolated, and one strand is still before the Registrar. The Company declared and paid dividends in Fiscals 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025 without transferring the amount to a separate scheduled bank account within five days of declaration, breaching Section 123(4) of the Companies Act, 2013; a suo motu application under Section 454 read with Sections 123(4) and 450 is pending before the Adjudicating Officer, Registrar of Companies. Form CHG-1 was never filed for the ICICI Bank vehicle loan, a Section 77 breach that may attract penalties under Section 86. Delays are disclosed across CHG-1, PAS-3, MGT-14, DIR-12, AOC-4 XBRL, DPT-3 and CRA-2. Statutory dues were delayed in every one of the three years - provident fund 3 instances / Rs 16.28 lakhs (FY2026), professional tax 12 / 9 / 3 instances, TDS other than salaries 11 / 6 / 6 instances, ESIC 1 / 3 / 3 - small in money, persistent in frequency.

Core process intellectual property sits with the Promoters personally, not with the Company. Under Design Rights Agreements dated May 27, 2026, Jignesh Panchal and Dina Panchal grant the Company rights to use the design 'Six axis multi location linear movement brazing machine', registered in India and the UK, for ten (10) years and 'renewable as mutually agreed' - so the renewal of a core manufacturing design rests on a future negotiation with the controlling shareholders. Four patent applications in India are filed jointly by the Company and Promoter Jignesh Panchal rather than by the Company alone, and four trademark applications remain pending; only one patent has been granted.

The register, the board and the payroll are all one family, with an outside layer six months old. Four Promoters hold 99.99% (Jignesh Panchal 1,50,95,970 shares / 95.62%, Dina Panchal 6,87,285 / 4.35%) and the Company has seven shareholders in total, three public holders between them owning 30 Equity Shares. Four of eight Directors are the promoter family, including Jugal Jignesh Panchal, 26, a Whole-time Director with 'over two (2) years of experience in the tubular components industry'. The fourth Promoter, Jubin Jignesh Panchal, 22 and 'presently pursuing an Industrial Engineering course from PennState College of Engineering', drew director remuneration of Rs 12.00 lakhs (FY2024), Rs 12.00 lakhs (FY2025) and Rs 8.00 lakhs (FY2026) before resigning as a director with effect from January 01, 2026, and remains a Promoter. All four Independent Directors were appointed on January 24, 2026, and the routed extract does not reproduce the board committee table.

Fiscal 2025 is not comparable to the years on either side of it, which breaks every three-year trend line in the document. Fiscal 2025 is restated on a CONSOLIDATED basis because Sai Ganesh Exports Private Limited was then a wholly owned subsidiary, while Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2024 are STANDALONE, Sai Ganesh having been amalgamated into the Company in Fiscal 2026 with effect from April 1, 2025 under a Section 233 confirmation order dated May 27, 2025. The break is visible in the cash flow: FY2026 states opening cash of Rs 36.00 lakhs, which does not tie to FY2025's closing Rs 47.84 lakhs. Any read of the revenue, margin or PAT 'trajectory' across these three years is comparing two different reporting entities.

The stated EBITDA does not reproduce from the restated profit and loss under the DRHP's own definition. Applying PBT plus finance cost plus depreciation and amortisation less other income to the restated numbers gives Rs 4,092.43 / 4,063.53 / 2,156.93 lakhs against the printed Rs 3,979.14 / 3,923.01 / 2,056.37 lakhs for FY2026 / FY2025 / FY2024 - a consistent gap in all three years, always in the same direction. The reconciliation sits in 'Non-GAAP Financial Measures' at page 358, which was not routed to this pipeline, so the difference cannot be explained from the extracted evidence. Risk Factor 50 itself concedes these measures are not standardised and 'may be calculated differently by other companies'.

The Sri City project's approval file is close to empty against a March 2028 commercial-operation date. Of nine listed approvals, only the APIIC approved-map application (letter dated 09-04-2026) has any status other than 'Yet to be received' - consent to establish, consent to operate, factory licence, certificate of stability, fire NOC, STP, PTRC/PTEC and the utilisation certificate are all outstanding, and the DRHP's own project note records that the statutory approval process 'is currently at an early stage' and 'company needs to expedite this at earliest'. Building and civil works are nonetheless scheduled to begin December 2026, before the consent to establish that is required 'before commencement of construction'.

Essentially the entire machinery package is single-country sourced from China at an estimated, not assessed, duty. Sanand's core lines come from Daiding Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. (Rs 1,393.81 lakhs), Shanghai Shenghe Precision Machinery Co., Ltd. (Rs 744.61 lakhs and Rs 536.61 lakhs), Zhejiang Changxing Heliang, Taizhou Jinghua and Yuhuan Weibang; Sri City's from Foshan Yishun, Zhejiang Huanjie and Suzhou Expedite. Plant and machinery is quoted at Rs 2,921.26 lakhs (Sanand) and Rs 1,117.53 lakhs (Sri City) plus 'estimated duty' at 10% of Rs 292.13 lakhs and Rs 103.41 lakhs, converted at USD 95.24 as of July 3, 2026, and the DRHP states the estimated cost excludes applicable taxes. Risk Factor 61 separately names tariff measures and anti-dumping actions as an exposure, and Risk Factor 26 names competition from subsidised overseas ecosystems.
strengths_observed: Revenue scale-up is real and continuous: revenue from operations Rs 30,170.42 lakhs (FY2024) to Rs 38,907.79 lakhs (FY2025) to Rs 46,808.59 lakhs (FY2026), growth of 3.33%, 28.96% and 20.31% and a stated CAGR of 24.58% - noting FY2025 is consolidated while FY2024 and FY2026 are standalone, so the middle year is not on the same basis as the ends.

The customer list is named, blue-chip and OEM-qualified: Daikin Airconditioning India Private Limited (Rs 15,623.49 lakhs, 33.40% of FY2026 revenue), LG Electronics (India) Limited (Rs 7,851.65 lakhs, 16.78%), Haier Appliances (India) Private Limited (Rs 6,870.94 lakhs, 14.69%), Bosch Home Comfort India Limited and Ecofrost Technologies Private Limited - with no order cancellations, product recalls or material quality issues in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 and no loss of a substantial customer in that period.

An external, non-commissioned validation moved the right way: CRISIL Ratings Limited upgraded the Company from CRISIL BBB/Stable and CRISIL A3+ (rated February 12, 2024 and March 11, 2024) to CRISIL BBB+/Stable and CRISIL A2 (June 6, 2025 and July 2025), with no downgrade in the last three Fiscals.

RoNW of 18.61% (FY2026) sits above both listed peers the DRHP itself names in the same table - The Anup Engineering Limited 15.98% and KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration Ltd 13.32% - on a smaller revenue base of Rs 46,808.59 lakhs against Rs 82,228.77 lakhs and Rs 60,005.77 lakhs respectively.

Backward integration into brass is now producing, not just installed: the Noida Facility 1 brass line went from 4,50,000 Nos installed at 0.26% utilisation (FY2024) to 22,50,000 Nos at 71.76% (FY2026), and import purchases fell from 45.18% of purchases (FY2024) to 25.26% (FY2025) to 9.71% (Rs 3,724.70 lakhs, FY2026).

Land risk on both Objects is already retired: the Sanand expansion sits on a contiguous 6,655.00 sq. mtr. GIDC parcel at Plot Nos. E-236 and E-237 held on a 99-year lease from February 23, 2018 with leasehold rights assigned by deed dated July 18, 2025, and the Sri City site is a 14,690.61 sq. mtr. APIIC plot at IP Mambattu Phase-II - both recorded as 'Land acquisition status: Completed'.

Receivables and inventory are tightly run for a 96.60%-top-10 book: trade receivable days 47, 43 and 49 across FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024, inventory days 60, 61 and 72, and bad debts written off of only Rs 26.75 lakhs in FY2026 (0.06% of revenue from operations) against Rs 1.19 lakhs and Rs 0.20 lakhs.

The exposure ledger is clean where it can be checked: nil Promoter shares pledged or otherwise encumbered, NIL outstanding litigation both by and against Directors (other than Promoters), Promoters, KMPs and Senior Management, and contingent liabilities of Rs 137.58 lakhs equal to 1.46% of net worth as at March 31, 2026.

The VRV line is the one mix shift that improved: VRV components rose to 13.94% of FY2026 revenue (Rs 6,519.77 lakhs) from 10.57% in FY2025, with product-wise utilisation at 73.79% against 54.56% and 52.35% in the two prior Fiscals.
